Using the linearity property of double integrals, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(6{x}^{2}-10{y}^{4})\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}6{x}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A-{∬}_{R}10{y}^{4}\text{ }\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the first integral is independent of $y.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}6{x}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(1-(-1)){\int }_{-2}^{0}6{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot 2{x}^{3}{|}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =2(2\cdot {0}^{3}-2\cdot (-2)^{3}) \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the second integral is independent of $x.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}10{y}^{4}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(0-(-2)){\int }_{-1}^{1}10{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\cdot 2{y}^{5}{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =2(2\cdot {1}^{5}-2\cdot (-1)^{5}) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, combining our results, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(6{x}^{2}+10{y}^{4})\,\text{d}A=32-8=24.\end{aligned}
$$
